questions.text_english:
(1) What do we typically do when we find our children doing something we don't approve of? We become reactive parents. Often, we pepper our reactions with lectures. When it doesn't work and predictably so; we end up screaming and dole out a punishment. And our children react with anger, resentment or 'can't-be-bothered' attitude.

(2) Buddhist Zen Master Thich Nhat Hanh put it beautifully when he described how each child has both negative seeds of anger, despair, hatred, fear and violence- and wholesome seeds of love, happiness, compassion and forgiveness. According to him, what will blossom depends on the seeds we nurture.

(3) A parenting and educational approach that's gaining a large following internationally, called the Nurtured Heart Approach (NHA) by Howard Glasser, is very much in keeping with this Zen approach. The three main aspects of this approach are: Refuse to energize negativity. Relentlessly energize their positives. Reset: Do not react negatively and stay calm when the child does something wrong. Parents following this approach commit to not saying or doing anything that may fuel negativity in the child. But the parent has to make sure she/he does this very calmly, without any anger or resentment.

(4) While on a mission to cut the negative, the parent looks for every opportunity to energize the positive in the child. This is done through persistently appreciating the goodness in the child in the smallest of ways: You were really generous about sharing your pizza with your sister; I appreciate the hard work you have put in your project; It takes courage to stand up to a bully. If you observe, the appreciation is not about saying excellentamazingor good which is really an empty praise and does not speak much to the child. Qualifying a praise, on the other hand, gives the child direction and she/he begins to understand what qualities, values and strengths are appreciated. These are also necessary ingredients of life skills and success.

(5) This approach is not merely about noticing when the child is being good, it is about recognizing the child's worth at every step. It's about aligning his energy in believing that he has great qualities, which are being identified and validated by the parents at every step. He realizes that there is no point choosing negativity, as there are no pay-offs in it. So, start building your child's inner wealth - there is nothing to lose.

sub_questions.text_english: Complete the following sentence with an appropriate word: we end up screaming and dole out punishment.In the above sentence, the author criticizes the _______ approach of the parents.
sub_questions.solution: The correct word is reactive. As mentioned in paragraph 1, the author identifies the behavior of screaming and punishing as part of becoming reactive parents.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain in about 40 words, when and how do parents become reactive.

key_points: Parents become reactive when children do things they disapprove of.
When that fails, they resort to screaming and punishment.

sub_questions.solution: Parents become reactive when they observe their children doing something they disapprove of. Initially, they pepper their responses with lectures. When these do not work, which is often predictable, they lose their calm, start screaming, and eventually dole out punishments to the children.

sub_questions.text_english:
In the line 'what will bloom will depend on the seeds we nurture' what seeds does the author refer to?
(A) Seasonal seeds
(B) Societal news
(C) Parental attitude
(D) Values and emotions
sub_questions.solution: The author refers to negative seeds (anger, despair, hatred) and wholesome seeds (love, happiness, compassion). These are values and emotions that reside within a child, making option D the correct answer.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain in about 40 words why does NHA focus on reforming parents to reform children.

key_points: NHA shifts focus from negative reactions to positive reinforcement.
Parents learn to stay calm and refuse to energize negativity.
By changing the parent's response, the child's environment improves, encouraging positive growth.

sub_questions.solution: NHA focuses on reforming parents because children's behavior is influenced by the feedback they receive. By staying calm and refusing to energize negativity, parents stop fueling the child's bad behavior. Instead, they nurture positive seeds, creating an environment where the child naturally chooses goodness.

sub_questions.text_english: Share evidence from the text, in about 40 words, to support the view that parents appreciate the goodness of the child at every opportunity.

key_points: Examples include sharing pizza, project hard work, and standing up to a bully.
This persistent appreciation focuses on specific qualities.

sub_questions.solution: The text states that parents persistently appreciate goodness in the smallest ways. Examples include acknowledging a child's generosity in sharing pizza, the hard work put into a school project, or the courage shown when standing up to a bully, rather than using empty praise.

sub_questions.text_english: In paragraph 5, in what way does 'This approach' differ from the earlier approach?

key_points: NHA focuses on recognizing worth at every step.
It aligns the child's energy by validating their qualities.

sub_questions.solution: Earlier, the approach was reactive, involving lectures and punishment. In contrast, NHA goes beyond merely noticing good behavior. It involves recognizing a child's inherent worth at every step, aligning their energy by identifying and validating their great qualities to build inner wealth.

questions.text_english:
(1) We're all familiar with the usual reasons workers cite for wanting to stay away even after lockdowns have long ended: flexible schedules, not having to commute, and of course, increased productivity. However, productivity isn't the only reason people want to stay away from the office. We recently surveyed 1,000 remote workers to find out what's really keeping them tied to their work-from-home lives.

(2) The findings include: 72% want to be able to take a nap or exercise during the day. Nearly three out of four remote workers surveyed stated that the ability to take a nap or workout during the workday was one of the reasons they wanted to stay home. Though these activities may very well increase worker productivity, there's no doubt that a nap on the kitchen couch would be frowned upon in the office.

(3) 73% want to be able to watch TV while they work. Three out of four respondents again say that being able to entertain themselves with TV, podcasts, music, or other media is one of the reasons they want to keep their work-from-home lifestyle.

(4) 62% cite concerns about their appearance. Well over half of respondents stated that they are concerned about their co-workers seeing them in-person again after such a long time apart. Whether it's weight loss or gain, not having the right clothes, or another concern about appearance, most would rather not have to worry about the way they look to their co-workers outside a Zoom call.

(5) When asked to choose the reason that most affects their desire to keep working from home, predictable answers like caring for children and lack of a commute were still the most common number one reasons. 14% of respondents stated that working remotely was so important to them, that they would not go back to work in-person even if their employers required it.

sub_questions.text_english: Explain in your own words how appearance is one of the factors for people's preference for work from home.

Fear of being judged by colleagues in person.

sub_questions.solution: Appearance is a factor because many remote workers feel self-conscious about their physical changes, such as weight gain or loss, or not having appropriate professional attire. They prefer avoiding the pressure of having their physical appearance scrutinized by co-workers in an office setting.

sub_questions.text_english: As per the survey, what top priorities of people prevent them from going to office?
sub_questions.solution: According to the survey, the top priorities preventing workers from returning to the office include family responsibilities like caring for children and the desire to avoid the daily commute. Additionally, the ability to integrate personal leisure activities like exercise, naps, and watching media is crucial.

Attempt ANY ONE of the two questions, in 120-150 words:
(a) With the advancement of science and technology, basic communication has adversely impacted the social skills of today's youth. You are Girish / Girija of class XII. sub_questions.text_english: Article writing
sub_questions.solution:
TECHNOLOGY AND SOCIAL SKILLS: THE DISCONNECT
By Girish

Technology has revolutionized communication, yet it has paradoxically left today’s youth socially inept. The constant reliance on digital interfaces has led to a significant decrease in face-to-face interaction, resulting in a lack of engagement and poor interpersonal skills. Many students struggle to initiate a conversation or read basic social cues. To combat this, the youth must prioritize real-world interaction. Engaging in outdoor sports, participating in collaborative school projects, and attending community workshops are essential steps. We must consciously create time for unfiltered, in-person conversations to develop the collaborative skills necessary for a successful future. By stepping away from screens and stepping into the real world, we can overcome social awkwardness and forge meaningful, authentic connections. The power of human connection must remain our priority.

sub_questions.text_english: Report writing
sub_questions.solution:
STREET PLAY ON EDUCATION FOR ALL
By President, Drama Club

On June 3, 2026, the School Drama Club organized a street play at Central Park, titled 'Education: An Equal Opportunity'. A group of twenty students participated, delivering an impactful performance focused on the importance of education for all children. The play was followed by an interactive session with the spectators, allowing the audience to share their views. Several star actors delivered powerful performances that captured the crowd's attention instantly. The local residents highly appreciated the initiative, with many offering positive feedback on the relevance of the theme in current times. The event was a success, effectively highlighting the need for educational equality while showcasing the creative talent of our student body. It was a proud moment for our school club to engage with the city community.

(ii) I was frightened, but not yet frightened out of my wits.Says Douglas. Which qualities of the speaker are highlighted in the above statement? (Deep Water)
(iii) 'See you soon Amma.' How are these words contrary to the speaker's emotions? (My Mother at Sixty-six)
(iv) 'And such too is the grandeur of the dooms; we have imagined for the mighty dead.' Explain the inference you can draw from the phrase 'mighty dead'. (A Thing of Beauty)
(v) What evidence from the text reveals that Rudyard Kipling did not walk the talk? (The Interview)
(vi) 'Soaf, you really should be sensible!' What does Jansie's advice to her friend Sophie reveal about their friendship? (Going Places)

sub_questions.text_english: Mukesh's attitude

key_points: He dreams of becoming a motor mechanic.
Unlike his family/friends who accept bangle making as destiny.

sub_questions.solution: Mukesh's attitude is distinct because he dares to dream beyond the ancestral profession of bangle-making. While his family and peers consider poverty and hard labor as their predetermined fate, Mukesh actively aspires to become a motor mechanic, showing hope, ambition, and the courage to break the cycle.

sub_questions.text_english: Douglas's qualities
sub_questions.solution: This statement highlights Douglas's presence of mind, courage, and composure in a life-threatening situation. Even while experiencing fear, he retains the ability to think rationally and plan his escape, demonstrating that he is not entirely paralyzed by panic, which is a crucial quality for survival.

sub_questions.text_english: Speaker's emotions

key_points: Contrasts inner fear with external optimism.
Words are a facade to provide comfort.

sub_questions.solution: These words are contrary to the poet's emotions because they sound optimistic and cheerful, whereas she is internally anxious and deeply pained by her mother's frailty and impending death. She uses this facade of hope to comfort her mother and herself against the harsh reality.

sub_questions.text_english: Inference of 'mighty dead'

key_points: Death is not the end of their influence.

sub_questions.solution: The phrase 'mighty dead' refers to historical heroes, ancestors, or individuals whose lives were noble and inspiring. The inference is that their grandeur lies in the great deeds and sacrifices they made, which continue to inspire and enrich the lives of subsequent generations even after their death.

sub_questions.text_english: Kipling evidence
sub_questions.solution: Evidence that Rudyard Kipling did not 'walk the talk' is his contradictory behavior regarding interviews. While he intensely disliked interviews, calling them immoral and cowardly, he himself had interviewed Mark Twain, showing he was not against the practice when he held the power as the interviewer.

sub_questions.text_english: Jansie's advice
sub_questions.solution: Jansie's advice reveals her grounded and realistic nature compared to Sophie's escapist and fantasy-prone mindset. While Sophie gets lost in daydreams, Jansie, being a loyal but pragmatic friend, tries to bring her back to reality by reminding her of their modest social background, showing concern for her friend's mental well-being.

sub_questions.text_english: Students on Ice Programme
sub_questions.solution: The 'Students on Ice' programme is a step towards the future because it exposes impressionable young students to the fragile reality of Antarctica. By witnessing the impact of climate change firsthand, they develop the sensitivity and consciousness required to become responsible leaders who will protect the earth's future.

sub_questions.text_english: Louisa's behavior
sub_questions.solution: Louisa behaves as a perfect wife by being genuinely concerned about Charley's well-being. Even when she initially believes his 'Third Level' story is a result of his anxiety or mental state, she does not mock him but instead listens and attempts to support him through his stressful situation.

sub_questions.text_english: Servants' reaction

key_points: They are loyal to Japanese heritage/patriotism.

sub_questions.solution: The servants were deeply outraged and horrified by Dr. Sadao's decision to treat a wounded American soldier. As patriotic Japanese citizens, they viewed his act as a betrayal of their country and felt it was wrong to save an enemy. Consequently, they rebelled and left the household in protest.

questions.text_english:
Answer ANY ONE of the following two questions in 120-150 words:
(a) After reading 'Aunt Jennifer's Tiger' and 'Going Places', you realise that Aunt Jennifer and Sophie's mother have been subdued by their respective husbands. As a social activist you have to write an article to a newspaper on the need to empower women. You may begin like this: Empowerment of women is a very essential social reform. It needs to be accelerated for any nation to progress
(b) 'A Roadside Stand' and 'Lost Spring' depict two contrasting worlds existing in society. Justify this statement with reference to the poem 'A Roadside Stand' and the text 'The Lost Spring'. You may begin: social satire in the two texts portrays two contrasting worlds that exist in society.

sub_questions.text_english: Article on Women Empowerment

key_points: Reference to Aunt Jennifer and Sophie's mother (subjugated women)

sub_questions.solution: Empowerment of women is a very essential social reform. It needs to be accelerated for any nation to progress. As seen in literature, women like Aunt Jennifer and Sophie's mother often live lives subdued by their husbands, trapped in traditional gender roles and domesticity. Aunt Jennifer represents the emotional confinement and fear women face, while Sophie’s mother embodies the silent, overworked woman resigned to her lot. These characters highlight the necessity of dismantling societal barriers that suppress female independence. True empowerment requires access to education, financial autonomy, and equal rights, allowing women to voice their dreams rather than living through the shadows of their families. Society must foster environments where women are viewed as partners rather than subordinates. Only when women gain agency can we achieve genuine progress, transforming households from arenas of control into foundations of mutual respect and equality.

sub_questions.text_english: Justification of contrasting worlds

key_points: A Roadside Stand: Rural poverty vs urban indifference
Lost Spring: Slum poverty (Firozabad/Seemapuri) vs systemic exploitation

sub_questions.solution: Social satire in the two texts portrays two contrasting worlds that exist in society. 'A Roadside Stand' highlights the widening chasm between the prosperous, indifferent city dwellers and the impoverished rural folk who struggle to maintain a living by the road. The poem critiques how urban growth leaves behind those whose very livelihoods rely on the city's flow. Similarly, 'The Lost Spring' delves into the grim reality of the urban poor in Firozabad and Seemapuri, where systemic exploitation traps children in cycles of hazardous labor like bangle-making. Both texts reveal a society where privilege and poverty exist in extreme proximity, yet worlds apart. While the rural folk in the roadside stand hope for economic mobility, the children in the slums are deprived of basic dignity and education. Together, these works expose the harsh inequalities embedded within our modern social structure, questioning the promise of development.

Answer ANY ONE of the following two questions, in 120-150 words:
(a) Mr. Lamb Lord, boy, you've got two arms, two legs and eyes and ears You could get on better than all the rest. Optimism is the best tool to face challenges in life. Imagine you are Mr. Lamb. You want to give a motivational speech to a group of differently abled students urging them to be positive in their approach to life. Write the speech on behalf of Mr. Lamb.
(b) Tiger population became extinct in the forests of Pratibandapuram.Tiger King is a typical example of man's dominance over nature. As a member of your school Eco Club, write an article for your school magazine on how man should follow the policy of 'Live and Let Live'.

sub_questions.text_english: Speech writing
sub_questions.solution: Hello! Dear Students! Believe in yourself. Nothing is impossible. Often, we focus on what we lack rather than what we have. But the world is full of possibilities for those who choose to see them. You have your mind, your spirit, and your own unique strength. Do not let society or your own self-doubt label you as 'differently abled' in a way that limits your horizon. Life is not about physical perfection; it is about the richness of your experiences and the kindness of your heart. When you change your perspective, you change your world. Challenges are merely tests of your resilience. Embrace your individuality, pursue your passions relentlessly, and never let the fear of what others think hold you back. You can achieve anything you set your mind to if you keep your spirit bright and optimistic. Keep growing and stay hopeful.

sub_questions.text_english: Article writing

key_points: Reference to Tiger King as a warning

sub_questions.solution:
LIVE AND LET LIVE: THE NEED FOR CO-EXISTENCE
By Member, Eco Club

The noblest principle, man should follow in his life is co-existence. The story of the 'Tiger King' serves as a chilling reminder of the consequences of man's hubris and his perceived dominance over nature. By obsessively killing tigers to satisfy his own vanity and ego, the Maharaja led his kingdom into an ecological imbalance, eventually leading to their extinction in his region. This is a cautionary tale of what happens when humanity ignores the delicate balance of the natural world for individual gain. We must move beyond the idea of control and embrace the philosophy of 'Live and Let Live.' Nature provides us with all we need, but it is not our servant. Protecting our biodiversity is not just an ethical choice; it is essential for our own survival. Let us be stewards of the planet rather than destroyers, ensuring that all species have the space to thrive.
